subject: Post-call recap: model fit, parity risks, and acceptance checkpoints
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Sara Huang <sara.huang@clearwave.com>; Maya Gupta <maya.gupta@clearwave.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: model fit, parity risks, and acceptance checkpoints

Hi Sara / Maya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have a shared picture going into an eval sprint: 

What we heard from your side:
- Primary flows: document ingestion -> entity extraction -> downstream scoring. Critical failure mode is hallucinated entities in financial statements.
- SLO targets: 95th pct latency <= 350ms for real-time scoring; batch throughput targets for reconciliation jobs.
- Compliance: audit trails and redaction controls matter for PII.

Initial Redwood hypotheses / asks:
1) Parity bar: you mentioned wanting to validate whether an open model can match your current proprietary baseline (vendor model). For this sprint we propose a parity checklist and explicit acceptance thresholds (see attached parity-checklist.xlsx).
2) Benchmarks & prompts: we'll run a 2-week trial with a 5k-sample prompt bundle (we included a starter set in prompt-sets-v1.zip). Please flag any additional document types.
3) Metrics to surface: top-1 entity F1, hallucination rate (false positives per 1k tokens), latency P50/P95, and token cost per 1k infer ops.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Action (ClearWave): confirm the 5k sample list and share one representative PII redaction rule (Maya).
- Action (ClearWave + Redwood): agree on the acceptance thresholds by EOD Friday October 30.
- Action (Redwood): Marcus will share model recommendations and expected perf/latency tradeoffs; Neha will publish the evaluation runbook and acceptance gates.

Attachments: parity-checklist.xlsx (draft), prompt-sets-v1.zip (starter prompts).

I'll consolidate this into the HubSpot deal record and send a mutual action plan once thresholds are confirmed.

Thanks —
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com
(attachment: parity-checklist.xlsx)

From: Sara Huang <sara.huang@clearwave.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Gupta <maya.gupta@clearwave.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 16:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit, parity risks, and acceptance checkpoints

Thanks Priya — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We can surface a 5k sample by Thursday; it will include quarterly reports, account statements, and a small set of noisy OCR scans. Expect some formatting variability.
- Our proprietary baseline has an internal metric we call "extraction precision" that roughly maps to your top-1 F1. Historically it sits around 0.92 on cleaned PDF reports, but drops to ~0.78 on OCR scans.
- Compliance: we'll provide our redaction rule doc (Maya), but legal needs to review any DSAs.

One ask: can you include a quick estimate of expected token cost delta for an open 70B quantized model vs our current hosted vendor? Even a back-of-envelope helps us justify a trial.

I'll loop in legal once you confirm the trial scope.

—Sara
Sara Huang
Product Lead, Data Platform
ClearWave Finance

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Sara Huang <sara.huang@clearwave.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit, parity risks, and acceptance checkpoints

Sara / team —

Quick technical take and model recommendations for the sprint: 

Recommended candidates (initial):
- Open model A: Llama2-70B (int8 quant) — strong with structured extraction, good latency with batching.
- Open model B: Falcon-40B (q4f16) — faster token throughput, slightly lower recall on nested entities in our early tests.
- Redwood-proprietary variant: rw-prop-13B-q4 — lower token cost but risk of lower parity on complex tables.

Tradeoffs to highlight:
- Quantization reduces cost but can increase hallucination risk in low-context / noisy OCR; we'll add a KV cache for document prefixes to stabilize results for long docs.
- If latency SLO at P95 is strict (<=350ms), we should run an early latency bucket test on your real OCR sample; some open models will need dedicated GPU capacity to meet this.

I'll attach a short matrix that maps expected F1 / hallucination delta vs latency and cost for each candidate (attachment: model-reco-matrix.pdf).

I'll plan a fast internal dry-run on a 200-sample subset once we get the sample pack. That will give a first-pass parity delta within 48 hours.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
(marcus.lin@redwood.com)
(attachment: model-reco-matrix.pdf)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sara Huang <sara.huang@clearwave.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit, parity risks, and acceptance checkpoints

Following up with an evaluation runbook draft and suggested acceptance thresholds. High level: keep the sprint narrow and metric-driven.

Proposed acceptance gates (example):
- Core extraction F1 >= 0.90 on cleaned PDFs (weighted by entity importance).
- Hallucination rate <= 3 per 1k tokens on mixed OCR samples (we'll measure by false-positive entity counts).
- Latency: P95 <= 350ms for single-request scoring on dedicated instance.
- Cost: token-infer cost delta <= 40% vs baseline for productionized config (quantized + batching).

Evaluation plan:
1) Dry-run (200 samples) — sanity checks, quick parity delta, identify failure modes.
2) Full run (5k samples) — compute gated metrics and qualitative review sets (30 red-team cases).
3) Regression check — run red-team prompt sets (in prompt-sets-v1.zip) to catch prompt-specific hallucinations.

Deliverables from Redwood: evaluation report (notebook + CSV), red-team cases, and a short decision recommendation. We'll provide the runbook link here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-parity-eval

If ClearWave is comfortable, we ask to lock the trial scope by Oct 30 so we can start the dry-run on Oct 31.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
PM, Eval & Model Fit, Redwood Inference
(neha.kapoor@redwood.com)
(attachment: prompt-sets-v1.zip)

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit, parity risks, and acceptance checkpoints

Sara / Maya —

Thanks for the quick replies and for committing to share the sample pack. Confirming mutual action plan and owners below so we can move fast: 

Mutual action plan (short):
- Oct 29 (today): ClearWave to share 5k sample list + one redaction rule (Maya).
- Oct 30 EOD: Agree acceptance thresholds (ClearWave + Redwood).
- Oct 31: Redwood dry-run on 200-sample subset; brief readout 48 hours after run.
- Nov 7: Full 5k run complete; evaluation report and recommendation by Nov 10.

Owners:
- ClearWave: sample pack + legal for DSA (Maya).
- Redwood: Marcus (model trials + cost estimates), Neha (runbook + report), Vivek (SRE: provisioning dedicated test capacity).

We will capture this on the HubSpot deal and send an invite for a weekly 30-minute sync starting Nov 2 to track progress. HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4892.

If that timeline works, I will kick off the DocuSign for the trial DSA and set up a shared Drive folder with versioned artifacts.

One more quick note on risks: if the open model misses parity on OCR-heavy docs, we should be prepared to run a fallback routing policy (vendor model for OCR requests) until we have additional fine-tuning or a small supervised adapter. Happy to scope that contingency once we see dry-run outputs.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Priya

Account Executive, Redwood Inference
